data: Planet Labs commercial Earth observation. PlanetScope (Doves) provides daily 3-5 m global; SkySats provide 50 cm tasked imaging.

Daily-revisit Earth imaging from two fleets — ~150 PlanetScope 3U CubeSats (3-5 m resolution global daily imagery) and ~21 SkySats (50 cm tasked high-resolution). All at ~475 km sun-synchronous orbit. The 'Doves' philosophy was 'launch hundreds of cheap small satellites, accept a few failures, get every patch of land imaged every day' — and it works. Planet's image archive is consulted by NGOs, governments, and journalists.
Only operational MEO commercial broadband — 20+ sats
Europe's civilian GNSS — ~30 sats, sub-metre positioning
Polar LEO comms — 66 operational sats +9 spares, GMDSS partner, global voice/data
Largest LEO broadband constellation — over 11,000 active satellites (as of October 2026)
First-gen LEO broadband — 648 sats in 12 polar planes

~150 PlanetScope 3U CubeSats + ~21 SkySats at 475 km sun-synchronous — daily-revisit Earth imaging. PlanetScope gives 3-5 m global daily; SkySats give 50 cm on-demand tasking. Every patch of Earth's land surface photographed every day.
An early Dove satellite, a flight unit donated by Planet Labs
